items.title: Shelly Berg interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 15, 2000
items.q: Michael Brecker showing a kid what a saxophone sounds like and try to get those values imprinted early.

ctx.x: Interesting, yeah. And you look at the audience that’s here and I mean these people are so into it, yet they’re all up there in age, and you’re going to wonder like are there going to be replacements.

I don’t worry about that so much because what symphony orchestras discovered, they worried about that too, that the audience is getting older and they’re going to just disappear. And what they discovered is that it’s not that it’s just this group of people in that age group, as people move into that age group their tastes change. So it’s always going to be a lot of people in that age group that gravitate towards those more artistic © Fillius Jazz Archive -12-

kinds of music. But I don’t think that that’s the total answer and I would like to see a younger demographic for jazz. I play at a jazz club in L.A. that is families and young people and college kids, and it’s straight ahead jazz and the place is packed every night. So that’s a hopeful sign. But if we can find a way to make people aware that that thing that’s all around them, that jazz thing is something that they can be consumers of, we can do a lot better.
